text: Pedro Antonio de Aragón (7 November 1611 – 1 September 1690) was a Spanish nobleman, military leader, and politician who served under Kings Philip IV and Charles II of Spain. He was the brother of Cardinal Pascual de Aragón, who served as Viceroy of Naples from 1664 to 1666, and the son of Enrique Ramón Folch de Cardona y Córdoba and Catalina Fernández de Córdoba y Figueroa. Born in Lucena, now in the Province of Córdoba, he was a well-educated individual who held several high-ranking positions at the Court, including Viceroy of Catalonia from 1642 to 1644, ambassador in Rome from 1664 to 1666, Viceroy of Naples from 1666 to 1671, and Commander in Chief of Catalonia. In 1670, he claimed the joint titles of 8th Duke of Segorbe and 9th Duke of Cardona following the deaths of his brother Luis Raimundo Folch de Cardona (January 1670) and his infant son Joaquín (March 1670), leaving only seven daughters. He was brought before the Justice Courts by two of his nieces and their husbands, but died in Madrid before the case was resolved, leading to ongoing issues regarding the numbering of the Dukedoms due to his self-appointed succession. During his ten-year stay in Italy (1662–1672), he built a personal library of approximately 3,600 volumes. As a patron of Poblet Monastery, he donated his library in 1677 in exchange for burial among its revered figures and sent back to Naples in 1671 the body of King Alfonso V of Aragon. He served as President of the Council of Aragon from 1677 to 1690 and published a work on Geometria Militar in 1671. This article about an Andalusian politician is a stub.
